questions.paperTitle: UPSC Civil Service Prelims Paper II 2023 (CSAT)

en.content:
Along with sustainable lifestyles, climate justice is regarded as a significant principle in environmental parlance. Both the principles have bearings on political and economic choices of the nation. So far, in our climate change summits or compacts, both the principles have eluded consensus among nations. Justice, in the judicial sense, is well defined. However, in the context of climate change, it has scientific as well as socio-political connotations. The crucial question in the next few years will be how resources, technologies and regulations are used to support the victims of climate change. Justice in climate is not confined to actions relating to mitigation, but includes the wider notion of support for adaptation to climate change and compensation for loss and damage.

Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical, rational and crucial message conveyed by the passage?

options.content: Climate justice should be ingrained in detail in the rules of all the new climate compacts/agreements.
Environmental resources are unevenly distributed and exploited across the globe.
There is an impending issue of dealing with a huge number of climate change victims/climate refugees.
Climate change in all its connotations is mostly due to developed countries and therefore their share of burden should be more.

en.explanation:
The passage discusses the significance of climate justice and sustainable lifestyles in the context of climate change. It highlights the challenges in achieving global consensus on these principles and emphasizes the broader notion of justice. This justice is not only about mitigation but also about supporting adaptation and compensating for loss and damage. The crucial aspect mentioned is how resources, technologies, and regulations should be utilized to support victims of climate change.

Option A suggests that climate justice should be detailed in new climate agreements, which aligns well with the focus on supporting victims and the need for fair resource distribution mentioned in the passage. Therefore, Option A captures the essence of the passage effectively.

Option B points to the uneven distribution and exploitation of environmental resources, which, while true, is only a part of the broader discussion in the passage.

Option C mentions the issue of climate change victims or refugees, which is relevant but does not encompass the full spectrum of climate justice discussed.

Option D attributes the main cause of climate change to developed countries and argues for a higher burden on them, which is a specific viewpoint but does not capture the broader message of justice and support mechanisms laid out in the passage.

Therefore, the most logical, rational, and crucial message conveyed by the passage is best reflected by:

Option A: Climate justice should be ingrained in detail in the rules of all the new climate compacts/agreements.

hi.content:
पर्यावरण-विषयक शब्दावली में धारणीय जीवन-शैलियों और साथ-साथ जलवायु न्याय को महत्त्वपूर्ण सिद्धांतों के रूप में माना जाता है। ये दोनों सिद्धांत राष्ट्र के राजनीतिक और आर्थिक विकल्पों को प्रभावित करते हैं। अभी तक, हमारी जलवायु परिवर्तन शिखर-वार्ताओं और करारों में ये दोनों सिद्धांत राष्ट्रों के बीच सर्वसम्मति नहीं बना पाए हैं। न्याय, न्यायिक अर्थ में तो सुपरिभाषित है। तथापि, जलवायु परिवर्तन के सन्दर्भ में, इसके वैज्ञानिक और साथ ही सामाजिक-राजनीतिक अभिप्राय हैं। अगले कुछ-एक वर्षों में यह निर्णायक प्रश्न खड़ा होगा कि जलवायु परिवर्तन से उत्पीड़ित व्यक्तियों को अवलंब देने के लिए संसाधन, प्रौद्योगिकियाँ और विनियम किस प्रकार उपयोग में लाए जाएँगे। जलवायु के विषय में न्याय, दुष्प्रभावों को कम करने की कार्रवाइयों तक सीमित नहीं है, बल्कि इसमें जलवायु परिवर्तन के अनुरूप अनुकूलन के लिए अवलंब और हानियों और नुकसानों के लिए क्षतिपूर्ति, की कहीं अधिक व्यापक धारणा शामिल है ।

निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन-सा एक, इस गद्यांश द्वारा व्यक्त सर्वाधिक युक्तियुक्त, तर्कसंगत और निर्णायक संदेश को सर्वोत्तम रूप में प्रतिबिंबित करता है?

options.content: जलवायु न्याय सभी नई जलवायु करारों/समझौतों के नियमों में विस्तार से बसा हुआ होना चाहिए।
पर्यावरणीय संसाधन पूरे विश्व में असमान रूप से वितरित हैं और उनका दोहन हुआ है।
वृहद् संख्या में जलवायु परिवर्तन के शिकार लोगों/जलवायु शरणार्थियों की समस्याओं का निपटारा करने का एक आसन्न मुद्दा सामने है।
जलवायु परिवर्तन, सभी अभिप्रायों में, अधिकतर विकसित देशों के कारण हुए हैं, इसलिए इसके भार-वहन का उनका अंश अपेक्षाकृत अधिक होना चाहिए।

en.content:
Sourcing food from non-agricultural lands (uncultivated systems such as forests, wetlands, pastures, etc) in addition to agricultural lands enables a systemic approach to food consumption. It allows rural and tribal communities to sustain themselves for the whole year and steer clear of natural disasters and season-induced shortfalls of agricultural food. Since the productivity of trees is often more resilient to adverse weather conditions than annual crops, forest foods often provide a safety net during periods of food shortages caused by crop failure; forest foods also make important contributions during seasonal crop production gaps.

Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical and rational message conveyed by the author of the passage?

options.content: Food yielding trees should replace other trees in rural and tribal areas and community owned lands.
Food security cannot be ensured in India with the present practice of conventional agriculture.
Wastelands and degraded areas in India should be converted into agroforestry systems to help the poor.
Agroecosystems should be developed in addition to or along with conventional agriculture.

en.explanation:
The passage discusses the importance of sourcing food from non-agricultural lands such as forests, wetlands, and pastures to enhance food security and manage seasonal and natural disaster-related food shortages. It particularly highlights the resilience of forest foods and their role as a safety net compared to annual crops. The primary argument is for a systemic approach to food consumption that includes non-agricultural sources in addition to agricultural lands.

Given this context, the statement that best reflects the most logical and rational message conveyed by the author is:

Option D

Agroecosystems should be developed in addition to or along with conventional agriculture.

This option aligns with the author's advocacy for an inclusive approach to food sourcing that goes beyond conventional agriculture by incorporating diverse ecosystems, which helps rural and tribal communities maintain food security throughout the year.

hi.content:
कृषि भूमियों के साथ-साथ ग़र-कृषि भूमियों (वनों, आर्द्र भूमियों, चरागाहों, आदि जैसी कृषीतर पद्धतियों) को खाद्य का स्रोत बनाना खाद्य उपभोग के प्रति एक तंत्रानुसारी उपागम को सुकर बनाता है। यह ग्रामीण और जनजातीय समुदायों को पूरे वर्ष निर्वाह करने और नैसर्गिक आपदाओं तथा मौसम के कारण होने वाली कृषिजन्य खाद्य की कमियों से बचे रहने में सहायक होता है। चूँकि, वार्षिक फ़सलों की अपेक्षा, प्रतिकूल मौसम दशाओं में वृक्षों में पनपने की प्राय: अधिक क्षमता होती है, फ़सल न होने के कारण हुए खाद्य के अभाव की अवधियों में वन-आधारित खाद्य प्राय: एक सुरक्षा जाल प्रदान करते हैं; वन-आधारित खाद्य मौसमी फसल उत्पादन अंतरालों के बीच भी महत्त्वपूर्ण योगदान करते हैं ।

निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन-सा एक, इस परिच्छेद के लेखक द्वारा दिए गए सर्वाधिक युक्तियुक्त और तर्कसंगत सन्देश को सर्वोत्तम रूप में प्रतिबिंबित करता है?

options.content: ग्रामीण और जनजातीय क्षेत्रों और समुदाय के स्वामित्व वाली ज़मीनों के अन्य वृक्षों को खाद्य देने वाले वृक्षों से बदल देना चाहिए।
भारत में वर्तमान परंपरागत कृषि प्रथा से खाद्य सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित नहीं की जा सकती।
भारत में गररीबों की मदद के लिए बंजर भूमियों और निम्नीकृत क्षेत्रों को कृषि-वानिकी पद्धतियों में बदल देना चाहिए।
परंपरागत कृषि के अतिरिक्त अथवा उसके साथ-साथ कृषि-पारितंत्र भी विकसित किए जाने चाहिए।

en.content:
While awareness on use/misuse and abuse of antibiotics is common knowledge, as is the impact of dosing poultry with antibiotics, the environmental impact of antibiotics-manufacturing companies not treating their waste has scarcely been discussed at any length or seriousness thus far. Pollution from antibiotics factories is fuelling the rise of drug-resistant infections. The occurrence of drug-resistant bacteria surrounding the pharma manufacturing plants is well known.

Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical and practical message conveyed by the passage?

options.content: It is necessary to put proper effluent treatment protocols in place.
It is necessary to promote environmental awareness among people.
Spread of drug-resistant bacteria cannot be done away with, as it is inherent in modern medical care.
Pharma-manufacturing companies should be set up in remote rural areas, away from crowded towns and cities.

en.explanation:
The passage focuses on the environmental impact of antibiotic manufacturing waste and its connection to the rise of drug-resistant infections. The most logical and practical message conveyed is the need for proper effluent treatment protocols.

Here's why:

  • Option A: This directly addresses the problem highlighted in the passage. Untreated waste from antibiotic factories contributes to the spread of drug-resistant bacteria, emphasizing the need for effective effluent treatment protocols. This is the most practical and relevant solution.
  • Option B: While environmental awareness is important, it doesn't specifically target the issue of antibiotic manufacturing waste and its impact on drug resistance.
  • Option C: This statement is too broad and doesn't address the specific issue of antibiotic manufacturing waste. It doesn't offer a practical solution to the problem.
  • Option D: This is not a viable solution. Relocating factories doesn't address the fundamental problem of untreated waste and its contribution to drug resistance. Additionally, it's not a practical or efficient solution.

Therefore, Option A is the best reflection of the passage's message: It is necessary to put proper effluent treatment protocols in place.

hi.content:
प्रतिजैविकों के उपयोग/दुरुपयोग और अपसेवन के बारे में जागरूकता आम जानकारी है, जैसे यह कि मुर्गे-मुर्गियों को प्रतिजैविक खिलाने का क्या असर होता है। प्रतिजैविक-निर्माता कम्पनियों द्वारा अपने अपशिष्ट को उपचारित न कराने से पर्यावरण पर जो असर होते हैं, उनके विषय में अभी तक कुछ भी विस्तार या गंभीरता से बहुत कम चर्चा की गई है। प्रतिजैविक फैक्टरियों से होने वाला प्रदूषण औषध-प्रतिरोधी संक्रमणों को बढ़ा रहा है। औषध निर्माण संयंत्रों के चारों तरफ औषध-प्रतिरोधी जीवाणुओं के होने का सबको संज्ञान है।

options.content: उपयुक्त बहि:प्रवाही उपचार प्रोटोकॉल लगाना आवश्यक है।
लोगों में पर्यावरणीय जागरूकता को बढ़ाना आवश्यक है।
औषध-प्रतिरोधी जीवाणुओं के प्रसार को ख़त्म नहीं किया जा सकता क्योंकि यह आधुनिक चिकित्सा देखभाल में अन्तर्निहित है।
औषध-निर्माण कंपनियों को भीड़भरे कस्बों और शहरों से बाहर दूरस्थ ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में स्थापित किया जाना चाहिए।

en.content:
Benefits of good quality school education accrue only when students complete and leave school after having acquired the gateway skills. Like one learns to walk before running, similarly one picks up advanced skills only after picking the basic foundational skills. The advent of the knowledge economy poses new challenges, and one of the severe consequences of having an uneducated workforce will be our inability to keep pace with the global economy. Without a strong learning foundation at the primary level, there can be no improvement in higher education or skill development.

Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the passage?

options.content: To become a global power, India needs to invest in universal quality education.
India is unable to become a global power because it is not focussing or promoting knowledge economy.
Our education system should focus more on imparting skills during higher education.
Parents of many school children are illiterate and are unaware of the benefits of quality education.

en.explanation:

It argues that without a solid learning foundation at the primary level, improvement in higher education and skill development becomes impossible. This leads to an inability to compete in the global economy.

Therefore, the statement that best reflects the crux of the passage is:

Option A: To become a global power, India needs to invest in universal quality education.

hi.content:
उच्च गुणवत्ता की विद्यालयी शिक्षा के लाभ तभी प्राप्त होते हैं, जब विद्यार्थी शिक्षा पूरी कर गेटवे कौशल प्राप्त करने के उपरांत विद्यालय छोड़ते हैं। जैसे कोई दौड़ने से पहले चलना सीखता है, उसी तरह कोई आधारभूत कौशलों को प्राप्त करने के बाद ही उच्चतर कौशलों को प्राप्त करता है। ज्ञान अर्थव्यवस्था के आगमन से नई चुनौतियाँ सामने आई हैं, और अशिक्षित कार्यबल रखने के गंभीर दुष्परिणामों में से एक यह है कि हम वैश्विक अर्थव्यवस्था के साथ कदम मिला कर चलने में अक्षम होंगे। प्राथमिक स्तर पर सशक्त अधिगम की बुनियाद बनाए बिना, उच्चतर शिक्षा या कौशल विकास में कोई उन्नति नहीं हो सकती।

निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन-सा एक, इस परिच्छेद के मर्म को सर्वोत्तम रूप से प्रतिबिंबित करता है?

The paradox of choice is illustrated by the story of Buridan's ass. Jean Buridan, the 14th century philosopher, wrote about free will and the inability to choose due to numerous choices and uncertainties. In the story, a donkey stands between two equally appealing stacks of hay. Unable to decide which to eat, it starves to death. Changes in technology and innovations such as smart phones and tablets only exacerbate our glut of choices. Constant connectivity and overconsumption of real-time data and social media can leave little room for self-reflection and rest, making decisions more difficult. Life is about choices. options.content: Modern technology enfeebles societal structure and makes life difficult.
Modern life is full of uncertainties and endless difficult choices.
We are influenced by the opinion of others and have no courage to follow our own convictions.

en.explanation:
The passage primarily discusses the concept of the paradox of choice through the story of Buridan's ass and its application to modern life. The key point is that having an abundance of choices can lead to decision paralysis and anxiety, much like the donkey that couldn't choose between two equally attractive stacks of hay and ultimately starved. While the passage mentions modern technology and its role in increasing the number of choices, the main focus is on the difficulty and anxiety arising from too many choices.

Given this context, Option D best reflects the most logical message implied by the passage:

In our lives, having too few choices may not be a good thing, but having too many can be equally as difficult.

This option captures the essence of the paradox of choice and the complications resulting from an overabundance of options.

Pharmaceutical patents grant protection to the patentee for the duration of the patent term. The patentees enjoy the liberty to determine the prices of medicines, which is time-limited to the period of monopoly, but could be unaffordable to the public. Such patent protection offered to the patentees is believed to benefit the public over the longer term through innovations and research and development (R&D), although it comes at a cost, in the nature of higher prices for the patented medicine. The patent regime and price protection - through a legally validated high price for the medicine during the currency of the patent - provide the patentee with a legitimate mechanism to get returns on the costs incurred in innovation and research.

Based on the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:

1. Patent protection given to patentees puts a huge burden on public's purchasing power in accessing patented medicines.

2. Dependence on other countries for pharmaceutical products is a huge burden for developing and poor countries.

3. Providing medicines to the public at affordable prices is a key goal during the public health policy design in many countries.

4. Governments need to find an appropriate balance between the rights of patentees and the requirements of the patients.

Which of the above assumptions are valid?
en.explanation:
To determine which of the above assumptions are valid based on the given passage, let us evaluate each assumption individually in context of the passage content.

1. Patent protection given to patentees puts a huge burden on public's purchasing power in accessing patented medicines.

This assumption seems valid according to the passage. The passage states that patent protection grants patentees the liberty to determine the prices of medicines, which may result in unaffordable prices for the public. Hence, it implies that there is a financial burden on the public.

2. Dependence on other countries for pharmaceutical products is a huge burden for developing and poor countries.

This assumption is not directly supported by the passage. The passage discusses the cost implications of patented medicines due to patent protection but does not address the issue of dependence on other countries for pharmaceutical products.

3. Providing medicines to the public at affordable prices is a key goal during the public health policy design in many countries.

This is also not directly discussed in the passage. The passage highlights that patent protection leads to high prices for medicines during the monopoly period but does not explicitly address the goals of public health policy regarding affordable pricing.

4. Governments need to find an appropriate balance between the rights of patentees and the requirements of the patients.

This assumption is in line with the passage. The passage indicates that while patents offer a mechanism for patentees to recoup their investment in innovation, it also acknowledges the need for balance as it mentions the higher prices and potentially unaffordable nature of medicines during the patent period.

Based on the evaluation:

Valid assumptions: 1 and 4

Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option B: 1 and 4

India should ensure the growth of the digital economy while keeping personal data of citizens secure and protected. No one will innovate in a surveillance-oriented environment or in a place where an individual's personal information is compromised. The ultimate control of data must reside with the individuals who generate it; they should be enabled to use, restrict or monetise it as they wish. Therefore, data protection laws should enable the right kind of innovation - one that is user-centric and privacy protecting.

Based on the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:

1. Protection of privacy is not just a right, but it has value to the economy.

2. There is a fundamental link between privacy and innovation.

en.explanation:
The correct answer is Option C: Both 1 and 2. Let's break down why:

Assumption 1: Protection of privacy is not just a right, but it has value to the economy.

The passage explicitly states, "No one will innovate in a surveillance-oriented environment or in a place where an individual's personal information is compromised." This directly links privacy to innovation, implying that a lack of privacy can stifle economic growth. The passage also emphasizes the need for data protection laws to enable "the right kind of innovation - one that is user-centric and privacy protecting." This further reinforces the idea that privacy is crucial for a thriving digital economy. Therefore, Assumption 1 is valid.

Assumption 2: There is a fundamental link between privacy and innovation.

The passage clearly establishes a link between privacy and innovation. It argues that individuals will not be willing to innovate or contribute to a digital economy where their data is not secure. The phrase "the right kind of innovation" suggests that innovation should prioritize user privacy. This reinforces the connection between these two concepts. Hence, Assumption 2 is also valid.

In conclusion, both assumptions are supported by the passage, making Option C the correct answer. The passage emphasizes the importance of privacy for economic growth and innovation.

In India, while the unemployment rate is a frequently used measure of poor performance of the economy, under conditions of rising school and college enrolment, it paints an inaccurate picture. The reported unemployment rate is dominated by the experience of younger Indians who face higher employment challenges and exhibit greater willingness to wait for the right job than their older peers. The unemployment challenge is greater for people with secondary or higher education, and rising education levels inflate unemployment challenges.

Which one of the following statements most likely reflects as to what the author of the passage intends to say?

options.content: Enrolment in schools and colleges is high but there is no quality education.
Unemployment must be seen as a function of rising education and aspirations of young Indians.
There are no labour-intensive industries to accommodate the huge number of unemployed people.
The education system should be properly designed so as to enable the educated people to be self-employed.

en.explanation:
The correct answer is Option B: Unemployment must be seen as a function of rising education and aspirations of young Indians.

Here's why:

The passage highlights that India's unemployment rate is influenced by the high enrollment in schools and colleges. This leads to a larger pool of educated young people seeking employment. These young individuals, with their higher aspirations and educational qualifications, are often more selective in their job search and may be willing to wait for the "right" opportunity. This dynamic contributes to the perceived high unemployment rate, even though it doesn't necessarily reflect a lack of jobs or economic stagnation.

Let's analyze why the other options are incorrect:

Option A: Enrolment in schools and colleges is high but there is no quality education. The passage doesn't discuss the quality of education. It focuses on the increasing number of educated individuals entering the workforce.

Option C: There are no labour-intensive industries to accommodate the huge number of unemployed people. The passage doesn't explicitly state that there's a lack of labor-intensive industries. It emphasizes the challenges faced by educated young people in finding suitable jobs, suggesting a mismatch between skills and available opportunities.

Option D: The education system should be properly designed so as to enable the educated people to be self-employed. While this statement might be relevant, the passage primarily focuses on the impact of rising education levels on unemployment, not on recommending specific education system reforms.

In conclusion, the author emphasizes that India's unemployment rate is not a simple indicator of economic performance. Consider the following statements in respect of five candidates P, Q, R, S and T. Two statements are true and one statement is false.

True Statement: One of P and Q was selected for the job.

False Statement: At least one of R and S was selected for the job.

Which of the following conclusions can be drawn?

1. At least four were selected for the job.

2. S was selected for the job.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Let's carefully analyze the given statements and their implications.

True Statement 1: One of P and Q was selected for the job.

This implies that either P or Q was selected, but not both. We denote this as:

$$P \oplus Q$$

where $$\oplus$$ indicates "exclusive or."

False Statement: At least one of R and S was selected for the job.

If this statement is false, it means the exact opposite is true: Neither R nor S was selected. We denote this as:

$$\neg (R \vee S)$$

which simplifies to:

$$\neg R \land \neg S$$

True Statement 2: At most two of R, S, and T were selected for the job.

This means:

$$| \{ R, S, T \} | \leq 2$$

Given the prior conclusion that R and S were not selected, this statement holds trivially, since T being selected or not does not violate this limit.

Let's combine these insights to address the options:

  1. At least four were selected for the job.

    This is not possible. From the analysis:

    - Exactly one of P or Q was selected.

    - R and S were not selected.

    - T can be selected or not.

    The maximum number of candidates selected is 1 (from P or Q) + 1 (if T is selected) = 2 candidates.

    Therefore, at least four candidates being selected is impossible.

  2. S was selected for the job.

    Given that the false statement implies neither R nor S was selected, S was indeed not selected.

From the above deductions, it is clear that both conclusions are incorrect.

The correct answer is:

Option D: Neither 1 nor 2

Let P, Q, R, S and T be five statements such that:

I. If P is true, then both Q and S are true.

II. If R and S are true, then T is false.

Which of the following can be concluded?

1. If T is true, then at least one of P and R must be false.

2. If Q is true, then P is true.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Let's analyze the given statements and the conclusions systematically:

I. If P is true, then both Q and S are true.

This can be written in logical form as:

$$P \implies (Q \land S)$$

II. If R and S are true, then T is false.

This can be written in logical form as:

$$R \land S \implies \neg T$$

Let's inspect the conclusions one by one:

Conclusion 1: If T is true, then at least one of P and R must be false.

Assume T is true. From statement II, $$R \land S \implies \neg T$$, the contrapositive is $$T \implies \neg (R \land S)$$, which means T true implies at least one of R or S is false.

Now combine this with statement I. From statement I, $$P \implies (Q \land S)$$. If P is true, then S is also true.

Therefore, if T is true, S must be false (from the contrapositive of statement II). Accordingly, P must be false to avoid contradiction since if P were true, S would be true, which contradicts the requirement that S must be false for T to be true. Thus, we conclude that if T is true, then P must be false, which logically supports that at least one of P and R must be false as S or R should be false.

Conclusion 2: If Q is true, then P is true.

From statement I, we have $$P \implies (Q \land S)$$. The contrapositive is $$\neg (Q \land S) \implies \neg P$$, meaning if $$Q$$ or $$S$$ is false, then $$P$$ is also false. This doesn't give direct evidence that Q being true implies P is true. Thus, we cannot conclusively deduce this conclusion from the given statements.

Thus, the correct conclusion is:

Option A: 1 only
